subject: Pilot technical fit + ops plan: model picks, benchmarks, and quant trade study
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@novamed.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot technical fit + ops plan: model picks, benchmarks, and quant trade study

Hi Jane — thanks again for a productive conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. TL;DR: two model families look promising for your summarization and triage flows; we'll run a short AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 trade study against your prompt set and the 10k-token benchmark to validate quality and latency.

Key notes from the call:
- Workloads: multi-document clinical notes (avg 6 docs, 5–12k tokens combined) and real-time triage chat (latency SLO ~ 150–200ms p50 for short queries).
- Data sensitivity: PHI in some fields — you'll use VPC private deployment for pilot.

Initial model recommendations (based on call and our quick bench):
- Candidate A: mosaic-13B-redwood-opt (quant-friendly, best cost/throughput for batch workloads)
- Candidate B: llama2-70B-chat-redwood (higher accuracy on instruction-heavy summaries; higher memory but may be viable with AWQ/FP8)

Planned technical experiments (proposal):
1) Promptset-led eval: run our 1.2k promptset (attached pilot_promptset_v1.csv) through both candidates; measure ROUGE/EM, hallucination rate, and latency/distribution of token generation.
2) Quantization trade study: run three paths — AWQ (int4/8 variants), GPTQ (8-bit), and FP8 where supported — record quality delta vs fp16 baseline. Focus on tail-behavior for long sequences; measure KV-cache growth impact.
3) Ops & throughput tuning: sweep batch sizes (1/2/4), KV cache warmup, continuous batching window; produce realistic cost/time curves.

Deliverables and timing (proposed):
- Bench report (bench_10kseq_results.xlsx link attached) with perf + quality matrices — 5 business days after we get confirmed prompt set and sample data (anonymized).
- Mutual action plan doc (attached) with owners and dates.

Immediate asks for NovaMed:
- Confirm pilot_promptset_v1.csv is the right evaluation set or send a revised sample (anonymized) by EOD Thu 4/13.
- Confirm target latency SLOs and acceptable quality delta vs current baseline (we need a numeric threshold, e.g., <= 3% ROUGE drop / <= 2% increase hallucination).

Internal notes for Soojin / Ben (cc'd): please stand up the AWQ/GPTQ sweep on dedicated-dev (g5x2 pool) once we get the sample. For the FP8 path, flag any known kernel gaps — I expect we may have to run a shorter sample for FP8 to validate stability.

Jane — happy to jump on a 30m follow-up if you'd like to walk through the MAP. Otherwise I'll assume we proceed once you confirm the prompt set and SLO.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0187

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@novamed.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 17:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot technical fit + ops plan: model picks, benchmarks, and quant trade study

Thanks Tessa — that summary is exactly what we needed. A couple quick items: 
- Confirmed: pilot_promptset_v1.csv looks good as a starting point. We'll strip PHI and send final sample by tomorrow morning (4/12).
- Latency SLO: for the triage chat we'd like p50 <= 200ms, p95 <= 650ms. For the batch summarization the throughput target is 25–40 qps for the nightly job.
- Quality baseline: our current internal model yields ROUGE-L 0.62 on the evaluation; if you can keep delta under 0.03 we're comfortable.

We're especially interested in the AWQ path if it preserves quality for the long sequences — cost is a big driver here. Please also call out any expected regression risk for hallucination with AWQ/GPTQ.

Thanks — I'll send the sanitized dataset tomorrow. If you want a quick follow-up call, 9am PT Wednesday works.

— Jane
Director, AI Products | NovaMed

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@novamed.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Apr 2028 06:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot technical fit + ops plan: model picks, benchmarks, and quant trade study

Thanks — quick technical readout on what I'd run and things to watch for: 
- AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8: AWQ (int4 variants) tends to give the best cost reduction for decoder-only LLMs with modest quality degradation on instruction tasks; the risk is highest on long-context summarization where quant error can accumulate in the KV cache. GPTQ-8 is usually a conservative middle-ground — better fidelity but less cost saving. FP8 (where we can run it) looks promising for reducing memory footprint while preserving FP behavior, but operator stability across kernels is still variable depending on the model family.
- Long-sequence behavior: measure prefix caching effectiveness and per-token KL/entropy drift vs fp16. Important to capture hallucination heuristics for segments after 2k tokens — we'll add targeted checks.
- Ops knobs: for latency SLO of p50 200ms, we'll start with 1-2 continuous-batch window and batch size 1 for triage path. For nightly summarization, enable batching of 4–8 with async KV cache pre-warm. We'll log per-token latency distribution to see tail impacts.
- Failure modes & fallbacks: plan an automatic fallback to the fp16-hosted variant for requests that exceed a quality/regression threshold (we'll annotate responses with a quality score during the pilot).

Action items for bench run (assign to Ben):
1) Provision g5x2-dev pool with quant kernels (AWQ/GPTQ) — target start 4/13.
2) Run sample set across Candidate A/B with fp16 baseline + AWQ-int4 + GPTQ-8 + FP8 (where feasible) and produce per-prompt quality metrics.
3) Produce a short tech note on expected cost delta per 1M tokens for each path.

I'll take ownership of the trade-study design and the QA checks for hallucination. Ben — can you confirm infra availability for 4/13?

Onward,
Soojin
Senior Applied ML Engineer — Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks Jane and Soojin. We’ll proceed on the timeline below unless you tell us otherwise.

- 4/13: Redwood infra run begins (Ben) — AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 sweep + fp16 baseline on Candidate A/B.
- 4/18: Bench report + cost delta + recommendation (Tessa/Soojin).
- 4/20: Decision checkpoint and pilot kickoff planning (NovaMed + Redwood).

Deliverable checklist in MAP doc (attached): per-prompt quality matrix, p50/p95 latency distributions, cost-per-1M-tokens estimate by quant path, hallucination-flagged cases with human review.

If 9am PT Wed works for you Jane, we’ll do a quick 30m to align on the sanitized data and the acceptance criteria. Otherwise we’ll stand up the runs and share the artifact links as they complete.

Thanks — will send a calendar invite for the 9am slot.

Best,
Tessa
